topic: Google Maps rendering transport: what decides it, and can a client choose

renderModes.name: canvas
renderModes.seenIn: WebGL denied, ?force=canvas, old UA, headless Chromium

note_firstPaintTiles: The ~24 raster /maps/vt/pb= tiles at ~275ms appear in ALL modes; they are the server-HTML first-paint grid and cannot be used to classify the mode.

q1_whatDeterminesTheArm.answer: The client. Maps selects a renderer in-page from client capability and client-supplied hints; the transport follows the renderer. No server-side A/B assignment was observed.

ruledOut.evidence: 21 distinct IDs across 67 trials; 0 exclusive to either arm; 18 of 21 present in 100% of both. 10212434: 7% proto / 4% raster. 10212435: 0% proto / 8% raster (2 of 25).
byte-identical in every trial and in all 5 pre-existing gate artifacts across both arms: EgoyMDI2MDgwNS4xIKXMDSoASAFQAw==
arm already decided with an empty jar; 12/12 re-navigations inside one profile with cookies present never changed mode
ruledOut.caveat: not a positive test of a specific cookie value

q1_whatDeterminesTheArm.speculation: The 1-in-36 stock-Chromium canvas fall is more likely a capability-probe timeout on a cold profile than a random server roll: identical navigator caps and identical ANGLE renderer string to the 35 mapcore runs, and it landed in the same canvas+labeler mode Firefox picks deterministically. NOT PROVEN.

mechanisms.notes: WebGL remains available (webgl2=true in all 8). An extension can do this with a DNR main_frame redirect.
Wrap HTMLCanvasElement/OffscreenCanvas getContext to return null for webgl/webgl2/experimental-webgl and delete WebGL(2)RenderingContext. Maps' probe is main-thread.
not recommended; breaks unrelated feature detection

warning.claim: Forcing raster does NOT by itself give a rewritable base map.
warning.evidence: WebGL denied + every /maps/vt/pb= tile URL rewritten to RoadmapDark: the tile bodies on the wire were genuinely dark (sampled 4: rgb(36.9,54.0,74.2) (34.6,50.8,72.0) (34.6,50.3,70.9) (31.0,59.0,76.2)) yet the rendered map was light, mean RGB (223.67,231.79,231.66) - byte-identical to the no-rewrite control. The canvas renderer paints from /maps/vt/stream/pb=...!4e1.
warning.whatDoesWork: Rewriting !1sset!2sRoadmap -> RoadmapDark on /maps/vt/stream/pb= : mean RGB (38.77,55.68,75.94), dark.

ruledOutDoNotRetry.result: zero base-map requests of either kind; broke the map
mapcore still loaded, zero proto tiles, only first-paint tiles; broken map

q3_stickiness.answer: Not a per-navigation roll. Deterministic for a given client configuration and stable across navigations within a profile.
q3_stickiness.confidence: high for 'not re-rolled'; medium for the residual rate
q3_stickiness.implication: Waiting for a lucky roll is not a strategy; a stock desktop Chrome user gets mapcore ~97% of the time and gets it again on every reload.

properties.auth: none - no cookies, no API key, no signed token

styleNameSweep.healthCheckSignal: clean 404 (~1620 B HTML) for a bad name - better than the raster endpoint's 178-byte yellow tile

evidence.condition: real MV3 extension, one static DNR rule, mapcore

negativeControls.condition: proto set: token rewritten to RoadmapDark on all 36 proto requests, legend untouched
negativeControls.meaning: the proto request's style token does not select the client palette

negativeControls.condition: legend swapped only, canvas mode without labeler
negativeControls.meaning: that mode takes its colours from the server stream, not the legend

notThePalette.reason: not keyed by style name; fetched identically in both arms
notThePalette.speculation: probably the shared style-transform program table the legend indexes into - NOT investigated

workingDnrRule.loopEvidence: testMatchOutcome on CompactLegend-RoadmapDark-<hash> returns no matched rules
workingDnrRule.verifiedLive: 5 fresh profiles, 5/5 dark, ruleset enabled and testMatchOutcome matched in each

trap.chromeError: Rule with id N was skipped as the "regexFilter" value exceeded the 2KB memory limit when compiled.
trap.whyDangerous: the extension loads cleanly, getEnabledRulesets() still returns the ruleset, and the only symptom is that the map stays light
trap.mitigation: assert chrome.declarativeNetRequest.testMatchOutcome() in tests, never just that the ruleset loaded
trap.bench: data/dnr-bench.json (5 regexes, offline, no live traffic)

whether the legend swap survives pan/zoom, layer switches, satellite/terrain or a long session - every measurement is a passive 14-15 s observation with NO gestures

precise size of the first-paint light flash with the legend rule alone (~1 s of server-HTML raster tiles)
